lesson: Do not hold overnight longs if the stock breaks below VWAP and the opening range with negative momentum; exit immediately.
Avoid long breakouts on stocks with concurrent negative news catalysts (e.g., legal settlements) even if technicals look strong.
In risk-off regimes, prioritize shorting high-volume breakdowns over chasing low-volume breakouts.
Require multi‑timeframe confirmation before taking momentum trades in a risk‑off market
Avoid entering positions when overall sector sentiment is negative, even if the individual stock looks strong
Set stops based on volatility (ATR) rather than fixed dollar amounts to reduce being stopped out on normal swings
Never initiate long positions on stocks facing major negative news catalysts (e.g. executive departures, guidance withdrawals, or regulatory probes) regardless of temporary technical bounces.
Do not buy earnings gap-ups on mixed reports where forward guidance or revenue missed estimates, as these setups frequently result in gap-and-fade traps.
Lock in profits early on news-driven short setups (like regulatory actions) rather than holding into the close, as intra-day bounce back is common.
Avoid taking non-catalyst short positions on premium travel names like BKNG without explicit technical breakdown signals.
For news‑catalyst shorts, lock 1R profit immediately to avoid a bounce turning into a loss.
For long entries, enforce a strict VWAP rule—exit if the price falls below VWAP before the close.
Avoid shorting on earnings days unless a tighter stop or higher conviction is justified; the volatility can erode gains quickly.
